name: Zaouia Ahansal
hero_subtitle: Historic spiritual sanctuary and stone granaries hidden deep in High Atlas gorges.

overview.title: A spiritual valley in the High Atlas
overview.p1: Zaouia Ahansal is a historic religious and cultural centre set in dramatic gorges. Traditional stone and adobe architecture and community life define the area.
overview.p2: It is more remote than Ouzoud or Bin el Ouidane and suits travellers with a vehicle and time for mountain roads.
overview.p3: Respect local customs. Combining with a guided trek or a stay in a village guesthouse deepens the experience.

moods.title: Zaouia Ahansal through the day
moods.subtitle: When to go and what to expect.

1.title: Morning light in the gorges
1.desc: Cooler temperatures and soft light on the cliffs — ideal for walking through the village and photographing the stone granaries.

2.title: Village pace and hospitality
2.desc: Share mint tea with locals, rest in the shade, and learn about the spiritual history of the zaouia.

3.title: Scenic return
3.desc: Drive out while the light warms the canyon walls. Allow extra time for mountain roads.

food.title: Where to eat in Zaouia Ahansal
food.p1: Meals are mainly with village guesthouses or simple local kitchens. Expect traditional Amazigh cooking and tea.
food.li2: Bread and tea offered as hospitality
food.li3: Limited restaurants — plan with your host
food.li4: Carry snacks for the road in and out
food.p2: Cash remains useful for small local places.

1.title: Access
1.desc: Remote mountain roads — allow time, prefer daylight, 4x4 helpful.

2.title: Respect
2.desc: This is a living spiritual and village community — dress modestly and ask before photos of people.

3.title: Stay
3.desc: Overnight in a village guesthouse for the full experience.

q1.question: How much time for Zaouia Ahansal?
q1.answer: Plan at least the duration indicated in the info box; longer stays reward hikers.

q2.question: Is it suitable for children?
q2.answer: Yes with supervision on paths and near water or cliffs.

q3.question: Do I need a guide?
q3.answer: Not always required, but recommended for valleys and remote tracks.

q4.question: How to get there?
q4.answer: By road from Azilal, Marrakech or Beni Mellal; 4x4 helpful on some mountain roads.
